# Tündük — Keepers of the Boz Üy

> Tündük supplies authentic Kyrgyz yurts (the Boz Üy) to hotels, resorts, and glamping sites worldwide. Not canvas tents made to look like yurts: the genuine article, hand-built in Kyzyl-Tuu, Kyrgyzstan, the village that is the world centre of the craft, and finished to a hospitality standard. The knowledge and skills of making Kyrgyz yurts are inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage (2014; the listing widened in 2025 to include the Karakalpak yurt).

## What a Boz Üy is
- The Kyrgyz tent, "grey house" in Old Turkic. A round, domed, demountable dwelling.
- Distinct from the Mongolian ger: the Kyrgyz roof poles (uuk) are **curved** and spring from the crown ring (tündük) down into the lattice walls (kerege), so the dome stands with **no central posts**. The whole floor is usable.
- Built from natural materials only: steam-bent willow frame, rawhide binding (no nails or screws), woven reed mats (chiy), handmade sheep-wool felt (about thirteen rolls per Boz Üy), and shyrdak felt carpets. The one optional synthetic is a breathable rain cover for wet climates, an add-on, never part of the structure.
- A 6m (20ft) Boz Üy weighs about 150 kg standing, lighter than a comparable ger or a Western engineered yurt, so it ships for less and clears customs more simply.
- Cared for, a Boz Üy lasts twenty to fifty years. Parts (a felt panel, a pole, the crown cap) are individually replaceable.

## Who it is for
- Hotels, resorts, eco-lodges, retreats, and glamping operators who want a real, UNESCO-protected structure rather than a factory tent.
- Finished in two directions: **Ak** (undyed cream-and-stone felt, the clean architectural reading recommended for hospitality) or **Oyu** (fully dressed with carpets, mats, bands, and a carved door).
- Sizes, named the Kyrgyz way: Jailoo (5m), Kochuu (6m, most ordered), Ala-Too (7m), 8m and larger by commission. Pole-free to 10m; 11–12m with discreet central support.

## How Tündük works
- **Pricing is quoted on a video call**, against the specification and destination. There are no published prices.
- Process: email first, Tündük evaluates the project, then a face-to-face video call.
- Freight and installation are handled under one contract, agent to agent, mostly by air. A build-and-ship cycle runs roughly six months.
- Every Boz Üy is checked by the maker Adylet before it ships.
- Tündük supplies a full materials and component data pack to support the client's own permitting and fire-safety review. It makes no fire-rating or structural-certification claims; formal certification must come from a licensed engineer in the client's jurisdiction.

## Honest boundaries (do not misattribute)
- Tündük is not a factory; it is a craft operation scaled with care.
- The felt is natural wool, not a treated flame-retardant fabric. No fire ratings are claimed.
- Tündük exports the architecture, not the culture: for hospitality it supplies the form stripped of ethnic ornament, and keeps the fully dressed, decorated Boz Üy in its home context.

## Origin
Kyzyl-Tuu, on Lake Issyk-Kul in Kyrgyzstan, is the village historically known as the centre of Kyrgyz yurt-making. Operations and export logistics (quality control, customs, freight) are coordinated from Bishkek, the capital.
